memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Avery selected the Thursday evening Delta return after the gallery confirmed a 4:00 p.m. finish, compared three currently available Denver hotels, verified taxes and mandatory charges against the employer’s $1,250 approval, and booked Delta plus a three-night Element stay without optional additions.

messages.content: The gallery has confirmed the Thursday review will finish by 4:00 p.m., so I can use the Thursday evening return. Please price the Delta plan that leaves Atlanta Monday and comes back Thursday, then find me a room for Monday through Thursday morning. The installation starts early Tuesday, so I need a dependable route to the gallery.

I’ll use the Monday, August 18 Delta nonstop from Atlanta at 11:05 a.m., arriving Denver at 12:25 p.m., with the Thursday, August 21 Delta nonstop at 6:40 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 11:32 p.m. Before I compare rooms, what gallery address should I use, and what is the approved amount for the trip?
The gallery is at 1200 Acoma Street. The approved amount is $1,250 for airfare, hotel, and one checked bag each way. Local transportation is separate.

The Delta Main Cabin round trip is currently $446. One checked bag in each direction adds $70 unless a waiver applies, leaving $734 of the approved amount for three hotel nights including taxes. I’ll check current availability around the Golden Triangle and along straightforward routes to 1200 Acoma Street.
Good. I don’t need to be directly beside it, but I do not want Tuesday morning to depend on a complicated transfer.

I found three available options for August 18-21. Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown Convention Center has a king room at $199 per night and $684.39 total with taxes; it is about 0.7 mile from the gallery, roughly a 15-minute walk or a short direct ride. Hyatt Place Denver Downtown has a king room at $214 per night and $741.12 total; it is about 0.5 mile away, around a 10-minute walk. Element Denver Downtown East has a standard king at $207 per night and $712.86 total; it is about 0.4 mile away, around an 8-minute walk. All three show current availability.
The Hyatt puts the trip over, correct?

Yes. With the $446 airfare and $70 in estimated bag fees, Hyatt Place would bring the covered trip total to $1,257.12, which is $7.12 over approval. Hampton would total $1,200.39, and Element would total $1,228.86. Those figures exclude local transportation, as requested.
Compare Hampton and Element more closely. Include cancellation terms, the actual room type, and whether arriving Monday afternoon is a problem.

Hampton is offering one king room, non-smoking, at $684.39 total. Payment is due at the hotel, and cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on August 17; a later cancellation incurs one night plus tax. Check-in begins at 3:00 p.m., so your expected arrival after the 12:25 p.m. landing should be fine even with transit from the airport. Element is offering one standard king studio at $712.86 total. It also permits payment at the property, with free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. local time on August 16; after that, one night plus tax is charged. Check-in begins at 3:00 p.m.
What does the Tuesday morning trip look like from each one if I need to be at the gallery by 7:30?

From Element, the walk to 1200 Acoma is approximately 8 minutes, so leaving around 7:15 provides a small buffer. From Hampton, the walk is approximately 15 minutes; leaving around 7:05 would provide a similar buffer. A direct car ride from either should take about 5 to 10 minutes in ordinary morning traffic, though pickup time can vary. Neither route requires a transfer.
Element sounds easier, and it still stays under the approval. Is there any issue with the Thursday flight if the review ends at 4:00?

The 6:40 p.m. departure is workable but leaves limited slack. From the gallery to Denver International Airport is commonly about 35 to 50 minutes by car at that hour, and Delta’s published cutoff for checking a bag is 45 minutes before departure. If you leave at 4:00 p.m. and go directly to the airport, you should ordinarily arrive with roughly 90 minutes or more before departure, but a delayed finish or severe traffic would narrow that margin.
I can check out Thursday morning and keep my suitcase in the gallery’s locked office. That way I won’t have to return to the hotel.

That removes the hotel stop and makes the Thursday plan more practical. With the suitcase already at the gallery, leaving promptly at 4:00 p.m. gives you the cleanest route to the airport. The flight fare is still available at $446 in Main Cabin.
Before I authorize anything, confirm the full numbers for Delta plus Element and make sure no optional hotel coverage or airline extras are included.

The current total is $1,228.86: $446 for the Delta Main Cabin round trip, $712.86 for the Element standard king studio for three nights including taxes, and an estimated $70 for one checked bag each way. That is $21.14 below the $1,250 approval. No travel coverage, seat upgrade, priority service, prepaid transportation, or other optional extra is included. The bag charges would be collected by Delta unless waived based on the payment method or traveler status.
Does the Element total include any destination or facility fee that might appear later?

The displayed $712.86 total includes the nightly rate, occupancy taxes, and the property’s listed mandatory charges. The booking terms do not show a separate destination or facility fee due at check-in. Incidental charges, parking, and optional purchases would remain outside that total.

All right. Book the Delta Monday outbound with the 6:40 Thursday return, and reserve the Element king studio for Monday through Thursday. Use the traveler and payment details on file. No coverage, upgrades, or other extras.

I’ll complete both purchases with the details on file and without optional additions. One final point: the hotel remains within approval even if both estimated bag fees are charged, but those bag fees are not prepaid in this transaction. Shall I proceed on that basis?
Yes, proceed. The bag fees can be paid at the airport if they apply.

Both reservations are confirmed. Delta is booked round trip from Atlanta to Denver: outbound Monday, August 18 at 11:05 a.m., arriving 12:25 p.m.; return Thursday, August 21 at 6:40 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 11:32 p.m. The charged airfare is $446 in Main Cabin. One checked bag each way is not prepaid and is estimated at $70 total if no waiver applies. Element Denver Downtown East is confirmed for August 18-21 in one standard king studio for three nights at $712.86 including taxes and mandatory charges, payable under the confirmed rate terms. Free cancellation is available until 6:00 p.m. local time on August 16; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. No coverage, upgrades, or optional extras were added. The trip total including estimated bag fees is $1,228.86, which is $21.14 under the approved amount.
